column1: # Design-system files copied from Binge, and where each came from.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Binge and this app share UI so the two look like one product, and the
# sharing is done by COPYING rather than by a shared module. That is a deliberate trade: a
# submodule is a lot of machinery for the ~23 files one companion needs, and this repository is
# meant to be readable standalone by someone writing their own companion. The cost is drift, and
# this file is what keeps drift visible instead of silent.
# It also makes the decision reversible. If a second or third companion app appears, the same
# ~23 files get copied again and the arithmetic flips toward a shared repo. Promoting to one is
# then a scripted move over this manifest rather than archaeology across two histories.
# FORMAT: four tab-separated columns, one row per copied file.
#   path-here            Path in THIS repository.
#   path-in-binge        Path in ScottCooper92/Binge the file was copied from.
#   binge-commit         The Binge commit copied at. Full SHA — an abbreviation stops resolving
#                        as history grows.
#   sha256               Digest of Binge's file AT THAT COMMIT, not of the local copy. This is
#                        the discriminator: a differing digest means Binge has moved on since,
#                        which is exactly the question worth asking. The local copy is expected
#                        to diverge and its digest would answer nothing.
# HOW IT IS CHECKED. Binge's `shared-design-system` skill can verify automatically — this
# repository is public, so Binge reads it unauthenticated. The reverse does not work: Binge is
# private, so nothing running in THIS repository's CI can read it. The skill here records
# divergence rather than resolving it, and says so rather than assuming the two match.
# Adding a row is a decision, not bookkeeping: it says this file is UX that should stay
# consistent across apps. A file that is genuinely this app's own does not belong here.
# path-here
# --- Nothing is copied yet. ---
# This app is a skeleton with no UI; the copy happens when the Seerr surfaces are extracted
# (roadmap stage 4 / Binge#1785). The manifest and its skills land first so the copy is recorded
# as it happens rather than reconstructed afterwards.
# Measured candidates, from the transitive closure of what the in-tree Seerr UI imports
# (Binge#2427). Approximate — resolved by symbol name, so a few may be over-matches:
#   AdaptiveLayout.kt  Dimens.kt  FoldPosture.kt  NavOverlay.kt  MediaAvailabilityUi.kt*
#   theme/BingeShapes.kt  theme/ExpressiveTheme.kt  modifier/SelectionLift.kt
#   component/: BingeTopBar BingeMediumTopBar BingeBottomSheet BingeSnackbarHost
#               BingeFilterChipRow ExpressiveIconButton TextEntrySurface AccountSettingsGroup
#               AccountActionSnackbarHandler* CarouselSkeleton EpisodeListRow MediaCard
#               MediaPagingGrid HeroCarousel RequestDownloadEta
#   * coupled to Binge's core:domain types and cannot be copied as-is. Both are integration-shaped
#     (MediaAvailability, AccountActionEvent), so they want the contract's generated types rather
#     than Binge's — which is the SDK's job (Binge#1786), not this manifest's.
